text: Radclyffe Hall's The Well of Loneliness was found criminally obscene by a court in the UK in 1928 because it depicted 'female sexual inversion' and pleaded for its toleration; the judgment kept it out of print there until 1949. In August 1928 James Douglas, editor of The Sunday Express, attacked the novel in an editorial titled 'A Book That Must Be Suppressed', calling it 'an intolerable outrage'.
